components.title: OneDrive (consumer + business sync client)

how.method: Official uninstaller: "%SYSTEMROOT%\System32\OneDriveSetup.exe" /uninstall (SysWOW64 fallback for Windows 10 only; Windows 11 is always System32). Revert is OneDriveSetup.exe /silent.
how.caveat: Leaves residual files; revert only works while System32\OneDriveSetup.exe still exists. Its docs claim 'you will not lose data, it is stored in the cloud', which ignores files not yet uploaded.

how.method: Guard before deleting %USERPROFILE%\OneDrive*: loops over HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\User Shell Folders, expands env vars, and ABORTS if any shell folder path matches %USERPROFILE%\OneDrive*; also refuses to delete any file or non-empty directory.
how.caveat: Only clone that checks known-folder redirection. Pattern is %USERPROFILE%\OneDrive* so a OneDrive root on another drive or a custom DefaultRootDir is not detected.

how.method: Uninstall string from Get-Package -Name "Microsoft OneDrive" (covers per-user and per-machine installs); refuses when HKCU\Software\Microsoft\OneDrive\Accounts\Personal or \Business1 has UserEmail; Stop-Process OneDrive,OneDriveSetup,FileCoAuth; run uninstall string -Wait; delete %OneDrive% only if empty (else open it in Explorer); stop Explorer; regsvr32 /u /s FileSyncShell64.dll; delete the install folder; clear HKCU\Environment OneDrive and OneDriveConsumer; Unregister-ScheduledTask *OneDrive*; delete %LOCALAPPDATA%\OneDrive, %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\OneDrive, ...\OneAuth, Start Menu OneDrive.lnk, %ProgramData%\Microsoft OneDrive, %ProgramFiles%\Microsoft OneDrive, %SystemDrive%\OneDriveTemp, HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\OneDrive.
how.caveat: Writes HKLM Winlogon AutoRestartShell=0 then 1 around the Explorer kill (3915, 3926): if the script dies in between, Explorer no longer auto-restarts. Does not look at redirected known folders. Unregister-ScheduledTask -TaskName *OneDrive* is a wildcard.

how.method: Install: OneDriveSetup.exe from System32 (current user) or /allusers (Program Files, machine-wide); if the file is gone, resolve https://g.live.com/1rewlive5skydrive/OneDriveProductionV2 -> amd64binary.url and run that; then remove HKCU User Shell Folders {B7BEDE81-DF94-4682-A7D8-57A52620B86F} and re-enable tasks "OneDrive* Update*". Both install and uninstall first remove HKLM policy DisableFileSyncNGSC.
how.caveat: Download URL is a Microsoft redirector, not pinned.

how.method: C# port of the Sophia logic (IOneDriveService). Uninstall: kill OneDrive/OneDriveSetup/FileCoAuth, run uninstall string, delete %OneDrive% only if user-file count is 0, AutoRestartShell toggle, UnregisterFileSyncShell, DeleteResources. UI accessor throws 'log out from OneDrive account' / 'user data folder does not exist' instead of running.
how.caveat: UserIsLogged() is wrong: it returns !(IsNullOrWhiteSpace(personal) || IsNullOrWhiteSpace(business)), i.e. true only when BOTH accounts are signed in (OneDriveService.cs:129). Port with OR semantics.

how.method: Script: Get-AppxPackage -AllUsers *OneDriveSync* | Remove-AppxPackage -AllUsers; read UninstallString from HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\OneDriveSetup.exe first, else HKU\<SID>\...\Uninstall\OneDriveSetup.exe (user install); run it hidden -Wait; delete HKLM/HKU Software\Microsoft\OneDrive (and WOW6432Node), %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\OneDrive, Start Menu .lnk, C:\Windows\System32\OneDriveSetup.exe, SysWOW64\OneDriveSetup.exe, C:\Program Files\Microsoft OneDrive, C:\ProgramData\Microsoft OneDrive (takeown + MoveFileEx delay-until-reboot), all *OneDrive* scheduled tasks; load C:\Users\Default\NTUSER.DAT and delete Run\OneDriveSetup + set Software\Microsoft\OneDrive EnableTHDFFeatures=0.
how.caveat: Header promises user data in %USERPROFILE%\OneDrive is preserved (line 19) but no known-folder or sign-in check exists. Deleting System32\OneDriveSetup.exe (line 374) removes the offline reinstall path that privacy.sexy and Sophia rely on. Script is also registered as a scheduled task (BloatRemovalService.cs:226-262).

how.method: icacls $Env:OneDrive /deny "*S-1-5-32-544:(D,DC)" (protect user files from the uninstaller); System32\OneDriveSetup.exe /uninstall -Wait; Stop-Process FileCoAuth,Explorer; delete %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\OneDrive and %ProgramData%\Microsoft OneDrive; icacls $Env:OneDrive /grant ...; delete %OneDrive% if empty and clear user env var OneDrive; Set-Service OneSyncSvc Disabled. Undo = winget install Microsoft.Onedrive --source winget + OneSyncSvc Automatic.
how.caveat: icacls /grant does not remove the earlier deny ACE (winutil itself uses /remove:d for Razer at tweaks.json:999 and 1032), so the Administrators deny on the OneDrive folder likely stays. OneSyncSvc is the Sync Host service for Mail/Calendar/People, not OneDrive; disabling it is collateral. Item lives in the 'Advanced Tweaks - CAUTION' category.

how.method: Treats OneDrive as an app with RemovalMethod WinGet: winget uninstall --accept-source-agreements --disable-interactivity --id Microsoft.OneDrive. Tier 'optional', not selected by default.
how.caveat: Needs a working winget (script warns if winget missing or < 1.4, Win11Debloat.ps1:331-347). No known-folder or sign-in check.

how.method: Stop-Process *OneDrive*, then run the uninstall string of the 'Microsoft OneDrive' entry (Get-ApplicationInfo). Script comment tells the user to copy/back up synced files, turn off folder syncing to get files back on the local drive, and disconnect the account first.
how.caveat: Manual precondition only; nothing is verified by code.

how.method: Runs OneDriveSetup.exe /uninstall from System32, SysWOW64 and Office\root\Integration\Addons; if $env:OneDrive is set it rewrites ~25 HKCU User Shell Folders values to %USERPROFILE%\... with raw reg add and then Get-ChildItem $OneDrive | Move-Item -Destination $env:USERPROFILE -Force.
how.caveat: Dangerous pattern to avoid: Move-Item -Force merges into existing folders and overwrites same-named files; raw registry writes do not create folders or notify the shell (Sophia uses SHSetKnownFolderPath instead: Module/Private/Set-UserShellFolder.ps1).

how.method: taskkill OneDrive.exe and explorer.exe, run System32/SysWOW64 OneDriveSetup.exe /uninstall, delete leftovers, set Wow6432Node policy DisableFileSyncNGSC=1, set CLSID {018D5C66-4533-4307-9B53-224DE2ED1FE6} System.IsPinnedToNameSpaceTree=0, then takeown + delete every %WinDir%\WinSxS\*onedrive* folder.
how.caveat: Deleting WinSxS content is unsupported and can corrupt component servicing; the policy is written under Wow6432Node\Policies which the 64-bit client likely never reads (unverified).

preflightChecks: Read HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\User Shell Folders (Desktop, Personal, My Pictures, My Music, My Video, {374DE290-123F-4565-9164-39C4925E467B} Downloads, {B7BEDE81-DF94-4682-A7D8-57A52620B86F} screenshots) and expand %vars%. If ANY value points inside a OneDrive root, BLOCK the uninstall and offer 'move folders back first' (privacy.sexy windows.yaml:35620-35745 does exactly this check).

Enumerate all OneDrive roots, not just %USERPROFILE%\OneDrive: env OneDrive / OneDriveConsumer / OneDriveCommercial (HKCU\Environment), HKCU\Software\Microsoft\OneDrive\Accounts\{Personal,Business1..n} (UserFolder, UserEmail) and folders named OneDrive* / 'OneDrive - <tenant>'. Compare each shell-folder path against ALL roots (privacy.sexy only matches %USERPROFILE%\OneDrive*).

Signed-in test: UserEmail under Accounts\Personal OR Accounts\Business1 (Sophia.psm1:3876-3878). Use OR; SophiApp's AND-style port is a bug (OneDriveService.cs:129). If signed in, require explicit confirmation that the user has verified sync is complete, or tell the user to unlink the account first (WindowsMize debloat.ps1:67-71).

Cloud-only and unsynced files: NO clone checks this (privacy.sexy and Sophia only test 'folder empty'). General Windows knowledge, verify before relying: walk the roots without hydrating and count entries with FILE_ATTRIBUTE_RECALL_ON_DATA_ACCESS (0x00400000), FILE_ATTRIBUTE_RECALL_ON_OPEN (0x00040000) or FILE_ATTRIBUTE_OFFLINE; those exist only online after removal. For 'pending sync', OneDrive exposes no stable local API: show a hard warning and ask the user to confirm the tray icon says 'Up to date' before continuing.

Install scope: per-user = %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\OneDrive\OneDrive.exe with uninstall key under HKCU (or HKU\<SID>); per-machine = %ProgramFiles%\Microsoft OneDrive with HKLM uninstall key and the task 'OneDrive Per-Machine Standalone Update' (Winhance OneDriveRemovalScript.cs:180-250; privacy.sexy windows.yaml:35954-36040). Per-machine removal needs the elevated helper and affects every user of the PC.

Processes holding files: OneDrive.exe, OneDriveSetup.exe, FileCoAuth.exe; Explorer holds FileSyncShell64.dll (shell extension), which is why Sophia restarts Explorer before deleting the install folder (Sophia.psm1:3913-3935).

Capture for the journal BEFORE acting: uninstall string + display version, HKCU Run 'OneDrive' and StartupApproved\Run 'OneDrive' values, scheduled tasks 'OneDrive Reporting Task-<SID>', 'OneDrive Standalone Update Task-<SID>', 'OneDrive Startup Task-<SID>', CLSID {018D5C66-4533-4307-9B53-224DE2ED1FE6} System.IsPinnedToNameSpaceTree (HKCU Software\Classes, + Wow6432Node), HKCU\Environment OneDrive*, HKLM policy DisableFileSyncNGSC if present, default-user Run 'OneDriveSetup'.
Other consumers: Documents\My Games or project folders redirected into OneDrive (game saves, repos), Office AutoSave targets, backup jobs referencing %OneDrive%. General knowledge, not in clones.
safeProcedure: 1. Read-only detection and preview (no changes). Show roots, sign-in state, redirected known folders, cloud-only count, install scope.

2. HARD STOP if a known folder is redirected into a OneDrive root. Offer a separate guided action 'move Desktop/Documents/Pictures back' implemented like Sophia Set-UserShellFolder (SHSetKnownFolderPath for the folder GUID and its library GUID, recreate desktop.ini, do NOT move files silently) after the user has copied/verified files; never use Move-Item -Force into the profile (ZOICWARE).
3. If signed in or cloud-only files exist: require typed confirmation; recommend unlinking in the OneDrive client first (this converts the cloud copy into a normal folder the user can keep).

4. Stage 1 (reversible, unelevated): disable Run 'OneDrive' through StartupApproved\Run (03 00 00 00 + FILETIME, WindowsMize Set-OneDriveRunAtStartup.ps1), disable the three OneDrive scheduled tasks, hide the nav-pane CLSID (System.IsPinnedToNameSpaceTree=0), ShowSyncProviderNotifications=0. Offer to stop here: this is the 'tame' mode.

5. Stage 2 (uninstall): stop OneDrive.exe/FileCoAuth.exe/OneDriveSetup.exe, run the recorded uninstall string with Wait (per-user unelevated, per-machine via helper). Do not delete System32\OneDriveSetup.exe, SysWOW64 copy, WinSxS or HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\OneDrive.

6. Restart Explorer once (normal stop and let the shell restart; do NOT toggle HKLM AutoRestartShell as Sophia does) so FileSyncShell64.dll unloads; verify the DLL is no longer loaded before deleting the install folder; delete only paths recorded in the journal and only if empty of user data.
7. Remove the %OneDrive% env vars and nav-pane entry only if no OneDrive* root remains; never delete a non-empty OneDrive folder (Sophia.psm1:3903-3911, privacy.sexy duringIteration).

8. Optional hardening: HKLM policy DisableFileSyncNGSC=1. Mark it in the journal because it must be removed before any reinstall (Sophia removes it at the top of both branches, Sophia.psm1:3858-3859).
9. Journal every value/file touched with its previous state; record the uninstall string and version so the restore can pick the same installer scope.
restore: Delete policy HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\OneDrive DisableFileSyncNGSC (and DisableFileSync) if WinModes set it (Sophia.psm1:3858).
Per-user: run %SystemRoot%\System32\OneDriveSetup.exe (/silent for unattended, privacy.sexy windows.yaml:35611). Per-machine: OneDriveSetup.exe /allusers (Sophia.psm1:3981).

If System32\OneDriveSetup.exe is gone (Winhance deletes it): winget install Microsoft.OneDrive --source winget (winutil tweaks.json:678; Winhance WinGetPackageId) or download https://g.live.com/1rewlive5skydrive/OneDriveProductionV2 (Sophia.psm1:3995-4000). This is the only restore path that needs network + winget.

Re-enable scheduled tasks 'OneDrive* Update*' and the Run/StartupApproved values from the journal (Sophia.psm1:4040); set nav-pane CLSID back to 1; HKCU\Environment OneDrive vars are recreated by the client on first sign-in.
User signs in again; folder backup (known-folder move) must be re-enabled by the user in the client.
breaksIfRemoved: Known-folder backup/redirection (Desktop, Documents, Pictures) becomes dangling if folders were redirected: Desktop/Documents may point to a path that no longer syncs or no longer exists (privacy.sexy windows.yaml:35634-35650).
Files On-Demand placeholders (cloud-only files) can no longer be opened; unsynced local edits are lost if the folder is deleted.
Office AutoSave / 'Save to OneDrive' / share links, Photos OneDrive integration, Windows Backup settings page (general knowledge).
Explorer nav-pane entry and shell overlays disappear (intended); a leftover shell extension can keep Explorer from unloading the DLL.
dependents: Any app or script using %OneDrive%, %OneDriveConsumer% or %OneDriveCommercial%.
Games that save to Documents\My Games when Documents is redirected into OneDrive; dev repos stored under Desktop/Documents.
Microsoft 365 apps (AutoSave), Teams file sharing, SharePoint library sync (Business1 account).

components.title: Microsoft Edge (browser, Edge Update, Chromium Edge)

how.method: Set HKLM\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\EdgeUpdateDev AllowUninstall=1 (DWORD); create a placeholder file %SYSTEMROOT%\SystemApps\Microsoft.MicrosoftEdge_8wekyb3d8bbwe\MicrosoftEdge.exe (the Edge installer checks for legacy Edge before allowing uninstall); run every "<ProgramFiles*>\Microsoft\Edge\Application\*\Installer\setup.exe" --uninstall --system-level --verbose-logging --force-uninstall (exit 0 or 19 = success). Revert downloads c2rsetup.officeapps.live.com/c2r/downloadEdge.aspx and runs /install /silent.
how.caveat: Edge only: the glob matches Microsoft\Edge\Application, not Microsoft\EdgeWebView. Not in any recommended preset. Docs state this relies on undocumented behaviour.

how.method: Same placeholder trick, then setup.exe --uninstall --system-level --force-uninstall --delete-profile. Undo: winget install Microsoft.Edge --source winget.
how.caveat: --delete-profile deletes the user's Edge profile (bookmarks, passwords, sessions). The MicrosoftEdge.exe placeholder is never deleted afterwards. Category 'Advanced Tweaks - CAUTION'.

how.method: First tries winget uninstall (Microsoft.Edge / XPFFTQ037JWMHS). Only if that fails and the user confirms ("NOT RECOMMENDED!") it runs ForceRemoveEdge: EdgeUpdateDev AllowUninstall (REG_SZ empty, 32-bit view), creates the SystemApps stub, runs the HKLM Uninstall\Microsoft Edge UninstallString + --force-uninstall, then deletes shortcuts, the stub and Edge autostart values.
how.caveat: Catalogue marks it 'unsafe': 'Removing this app also removes the only browser from Windows Sandbox and could affect other apps'. Cleaner than the others because it deletes its own stub.

how.method: Removes Chromium Edge via the HKLM\WOW6432Node Uninstall strings (+ --force-uninstall --silent, or msiexec /quiet for MSI), then EdgeUpdate via MicrosoftEdgeUpdate.exe /unregsvc and /uninstall, but first exports HKLM\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\EdgeUpdate\ClientState and re-imports it afterwards. Header states "EdgeWebView2 is NOT removed" and the folder cleanup explicitly excludes *EdgeWebView*. Installs an ie_to_edge_stub redirect (IFEO filter) so microsoft-edge: links open the default browser, and registers a startup scheduled task EdgeRemoval that re-runs the removal.
how.caveat: Marked HasInstabilityWarning. Best WebView2 hygiene of all clones, but still unregisters EdgeUpdate (WebView2 then stops auto-updating, privacy.sexy windows.yaml:9578-9600), deletes every Edge* / *Temp* folder under Program Files (x86)\Microsoft, and wipes all scheduled tasks matching *Edge*.

how.method: Remove-ApplicationPackage Microsoft.MicrosoftEdge.Stable, then the same AllowUninstall (EdgeUpdateDev, SZ empty) + SystemApps stub + '<UninstallString> --force-uninstall' (credits ave9858 gist).
how.caveat: Stub left in place.

how.method: EdgeRemove.ps1: temporarily sets HKU\.DEFAULT\Control Panel\International\Geo Nation=244/Name=US, runs the uninstall string through a copy of cmd.exe renamed dllhost.exe, clears NoRemove/NoModify/NoRepair on the Uninstall keys, then deletes Microsoft\EdgeUpdate under EVERY HKCU/HKLM SOFTWARE hive (incl. WOW6432Node) and unregisters MicrosoftEdgeUpdate* tasks. Optional -Webview switch also runs MicrosoftEdgeUpdate.exe /unregsvc + /uninstall and deletes the EdgeWebView uninstall keys.
how.caveat: Line 207 runs even without -Webview and removes HKLM\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\EdgeUpdate, the key Winhance backs up 'or else webview won't work' (Winhance EdgeRemovalScript.cs:402). Treat as a WebView2-breaking method.

how.method: archive/remove_edge.bat runs EdgeWebView\...\setup.exe --uninstall --force-uninstall --msedgewebview --system-level, then Edge and EdgeCore setup.exe --msedge; sets DoNotUpdateToEdgeWithChromium=1.
how.caveat: Explicitly removes the WebView2 runtime together with Edge. README (line 393-416) instead recommends only blocking profile creation.

how.method: Offers a separate yes/no 'Remove WebView2 Runtime?' with its own removal routine (see component webview2).
how.caveat: Shows how easily Edge cleanup scripts also take WebView2 out.

preflightChecks: WinModes should NEVER uninstall Edge (hard blocklist). If a user insists, the only acceptable path is a documented, journaled, Edge-only removal that leaves HKLM\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\EdgeUpdate (Clients + ClientState), Program Files (x86)\Microsoft\EdgeUpdate and Microsoft\EdgeWebView untouched. Not recommended.

Check for dependents before tame-mode changes: default browser/HTTP(S)/PDF handlers (UserChoice ProgIds MSEdgeHTM / MSEdgePDF), Windows Sandbox in use, installed Edge PWAs, enterprise/Intune policies already present (policies show 'managed by your organization', privacy.sexy windows.yaml:9316 and 9650).
Detect the WebView2 runtime separately (HKLM\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\EdgeUpdate\Clients\{F3017226-FE2A-4295-8BDF-00C3A9A7E4C5} pv value) and show it as 'not part of Edge'.
safeProcedure: 1. Offer policy-based taming only (see settingsInstead): disable ads/recommendations/shopping/rewards/AI sidebar, stop desktop shortcut creation, optionally block Edge auto-launch/startup.
2. Do not touch EdgeUpdate services/tasks beyond Manual: disabling edgeupdate/edgeupdatem or blocking MicrosoftEdgeUpdate.exe also stops WebView2 updates (privacy.sexy windows.yaml:9464-9600).
3. Do not set EdgeUpdate Install{...}=0 or InstallDefault=0 (it would block reinstalling Edge and, with the WebView2 GUID, WebView2).
4. Never write Image File Execution Options entries for msedge.exe (Winhance removes legacy msedge.exe IFEO 'to prevent Edge reinstall issues', EdgeRemovalScript.cs:302-303).
5. Journal each policy value with its previous state; reverting = delete the policy value.
restore: Policies: delete the values WinModes created under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge and ...\EdgeUpdate.

If a user ran another tool that removed Edge: winget install Microsoft.Edge --source winget (winutil UndoScript, tweaks.json:608), or Winhance MsStoreId XPFFTQ037JWMHS, or privacy.sexy revert (download c2rsetup.officeapps.live.com ... /install /silent, windows.yaml:36138-36150). Sophia re-installs Edge when removed by 'harmful tweakers' because WebView2 is required (CHANGELOG.md:858).
Delete the leftover placeholder %SystemRoot%\SystemApps\Microsoft.MicrosoftEdge_8wekyb3d8bbwe\MicrosoftEdge.exe if it exists (Win11Debloat removes it, Invoke-ForceRemoveEdge.ps1:56).
breaksIfRemoved: Windows Sandbox loses its only browser (Win11Debloat Config/Apps.json:685-691).
microsoft-edge: protocol links used by Search, Widgets, Copilot, Settings (Winhance had to install a redirect stub, EdgeRemovalScript.cs:299-303, 636-643).
Default handlers for .htm/.html/.pdf/.svg/.webp/mailto/http(s) remain registered to MSEdgeHTM/MSEdgePDF until cleaned (privacy.sexy windows.yaml:36162-36260).

Third-party apps and Windows features built on WebView2 if the removal also hits EdgeUpdate/EdgeWebView (optimizerDuck lists Edge as 'tied to WebView2-based apps and Windows features', Common/Helpers/Shared.cs:172-174; equk windows_10/README.md:113).

Edge returns after Windows Update / EdgeUpdate runs; tools respond with startup tasks (Winhance) or DoNotUpdateToEdgeWithChromium (privacy.sexy windows.yaml:9825-9840). privacy.sexy issue #309 'Edge still alive after removal' is cited at windows.yaml:9456.
dependents: Windows Sandbox, Widgets/Search/Copilot links, PWAs, WebView2-based apps (via the shared EdgeUpdate registration), Teams/Outlook (new) web components.

components.title: Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime (evergreen) and Windows' own WebView2 users

how.method: Blocks automatic installation with HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\EdgeUpdate Install{F3017226-FE2A-4295-8BDF-00C3A9A7E4C5}=0 and states WebView2 shares the Edge Update mechanism; separate item blocks/soft-deletes MicrosoftEdgeUpdate.exe which "is also responsible for updating Edge WebView2".
how.caveat: Pure policy/file blocks, but they freeze WebView2 at its current version (security risk) and a blocked Install policy can make app installers that bootstrap WebView2 fail.

how.method: Optional "Remove WebView2 Runtime?": NoRemove=0 on the Microsoft EdgeWebView Uninstall keys, EdgeWebView\Application\*\Installer\setup.exe --uninstall --msedgewebview --system-level --verbose-logging --force-uninstall, policies Install/Update{F3017226-...}=0, delete Clients\{F3017226-...}, takeown + rmdir Program Files (x86)\Microsoft\EdgeWebView and %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\EdgeWebView, and (when Edge is gone) EdgeUpdate. Prompt text: "WebView2 is required for many UWP/Win32 apps ... Removing it may break apps (e.g., Teams, Edge-based apps)".
how.caveat: Also taskkills SearchHost.exe (Start/Search host) before deleting, which shows Windows Search uses it.

how.method: remove_edge.bat uninstalls EdgeWebView with --msedgewebview before Edge.
how.caveat: Removes WebView2 together with Edge.

how.method: -Webview option runs MicrosoftEdgeUpdate.exe /unregsvc + /uninstall and deletes the Microsoft EdgeWebView uninstall keys; also removes appx Win32WebViewHost.
how.caveat: Opt-in checkbox, but the EdgeUpdate registry wipe at :207 happens regardless.

how.method: Never removes it: script header 'EdgeWebView2 is NOT removed', cleanup filter excludes *EdgeWebView*, EdgeUpdate ClientState is exported before and imported after EdgeUpdate removal, and WebView2 is offered as an installable app (winget Microsoft.EdgeWebView2Runtime, choco webview2-runtime).
how.caveat: Reference behaviour for WinModes.

how.method: Check phase reinstalls Edge if a 'harmful tweaker' removed it, because WebView2 is a mandatory Windows component.

preflightChecks: Detect, never modify: HKLM\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\EdgeUpdate\Clients\{F3017226-FE2A-4295-8BDF-00C3A9A7E4C5} (pv = version), folder %ProgramFiles(x86)%\Microsoft\EdgeWebView\Application\<ver>\msedgewebview2.exe, uninstall key 'Microsoft EdgeWebView'.

Any action that touches HKLM\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\EdgeUpdate, Program Files (x86)\Microsoft\EdgeUpdate, EdgeUpdate scheduled tasks (MicrosoftEdgeUpdateTaskMachineCore/UA) or services edgeupdate/edgeupdatem must be blocked or at least require 'this also affects WebView2'.
safeProcedure: No removal. If the runtime is missing, offer repair: winget install Microsoft.EdgeWebView2Runtime (Winhance ExternalAppDefinitions.Browsers.cs:27) or the Evergreen bootstrapper.

Memory tuning WITHOUT removal: killing msedgewebview2.exe is pointless (Batlez admits embedded apps respawn it, Batlez-Tweaks.bat:7927); the only supported-ish lever is the undocumented Start/Search feature override (see settingsInstead), labelled experimental.
restore: winget install Microsoft.EdgeWebView2Runtime; or run the Evergreen Bootstrapper; remove policies EdgeUpdate Install{F3017226-...} / Update{F3017226-...} if set (Batlez sets both to 0, Batlez-Tweaks.bat:23006-23007); re-import EdgeUpdate ClientState if a backup exists (Winhance pattern).

notes: Read-only study of the clones under D:\tmp\oss; nothing executed. Evidence is repository-relative path:line as read on disk (line numbers can drift with upstream; clones are shallow). Items flagged 'general knowledge' (cloud-only file attributes, Gaming Services role, Office AutoSave) are NOT in the clones and need verification on a test machine before WinModes relies on them. Decisions suggested for WinModes: (1) OneDrive = offer-with-safeguards with a hard stop when any User Shell Folder points into any OneDrive root, sign-in confirmation, a cloud-only count, per-user vs per-machine detection, reversible stage 1 (autostart/tasks/nav pane) before stage 2 (uninstall), and no deletion of System32\OneDriveSetup.exe, WinSxS or non-empty folders. (2) Edge and WebView2 = policy-only and never-touch respectively; do not edit EdgeUpdate registry, services, tasks or exe; show WebView2 as a protected dependency of Start/Search, Widgets, Copilot, new Teams/Outlook and third-party apps. (3) Copilot/Recall/Widgets/Cortana/Phone Link/Teams/Office Hub = policies first, current-user AppX removal second, record PackageFamilyName+InstallLocation+Store id, restore by Add-AppxPackage -Register / -RegisterByFamilyName then winget msstore id (the sequence winutil and privacy.sexy use). Never use deprovisioning, EndOfLife/Deprovisioned keys, TrustedInstaller tricks or CBS edits. (4) Store, App Installer, the Store service chain (AppXSvc, ClipSVC, wlidsvc, InstallService, LicenseManager, camsvc), \InstallService tasks, Windows Terminal, Defender, Firewall and Windows Update stay on the hard blocklist; WinModes services stay Manual. (5) Xbox: settings-level Game Bar neutralisation is safe; keep GamingServices, GamingApp, XboxIdentityProvider, Xbox.TCUI, XboxSpeechToTextOverlay protected. Extra top-level key 'wingetHandling' summarises how each tool treats winget and the Store chain. Not covered: Windows 10-only components (Edge Legacy, Cortana app internals) beyond what the clones show; Microsoft Learn documentation was not consulted (no web access used).
